subject: Accenture logo, current (2020-) version: black 'accenture' wordmark with the purple '>' greater-than mark (#A100FF). Transparent background.
license: Public domain (PD-textlogo on Commons: simple text and geometric shapes, below the threshold of originality). Registered trademark of Accenture; trademark rules still apply.
author: Accenture
notes: Vector, so it scales to any size. This is the version in use during 2020-2023. The '>' is Accenture purple, and the site bans purple, so the logo would be the only purple on the page. Brand guidelines don't allow recolouring the mark, so use it as-is or use it small. A black wordmark won't show on the obsidian ground; use the reversed variant there.

subject: Same logo with the wordmark filled white for dark backgrounds; the '>' stays #A100FF.
author: Accenture; white fill applied locally (one style attribute on the wordmark path)
notes: Derived file. Accenture publishes its own reversed (white) logo for dark backgrounds, so this matches an official treatment, but it was made locally rather than downloaded. Probably the one to use on the obsidian ground.

subject: PNG render of accenture_logo_2020.svg, transparent background.
author: Accenture; rasterised locally with headless Chrome
notes: For when a raster file is needed. Prefer the SVG.

subject: PNG render of the reversed (white wordmark) variant, transparent background.
author: Accenture; white fill and rasterisation done locally

subject: Wide shot of about 15 numbered storage robots (005, 009, 019, 097 ...) running on a cube-storage grid inside a warehouse hall. Red and black robots, red roof beams.
author: Euku (Wikimedia Commons user)
notes: The strongest 'fleet on one floor' image: many robots, each with a visible fleet number, which suits 'kept the fleet healthy'. Warm red tones sit well with the ember palette. 4:3, 2.2 MB; crop to 16:9 if needed. The small 'AutoStore' marks on the robots name the equipment maker, not a warehouse operator, so nothing points to the NDA client. Caveat: these are grid robots running on rails, not free-roaming AMRs. Credit line: 'Photo: Euku, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons'. Under SA, a cropped or edited version must also be released under CC BY-SA.
